items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: You know that’s Clifford Brown. ... I would play something out of the exercise books and it would sound like — hey that sounds like something Clifford Brown would use or play because he had that classical background.

ctx.x: Isn’t it amazing how you take a piece of brass and most trumpets are basically the same, you know you can have a little bit different mouthpiece but you listen to the difference in one trumpet player to the next, it’s just unbelievable. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Yeah man. I think that has to do with the concept — first of all I think the sound is already there, no matter what you play on, it’s in your head. And that’s what I try — no matter what, if I’m playing somebody’s instrument I’m trying to hear that and that’s the way I’m going to hear it. I have some friends of mine, one guy in particular was a saxophone player, he comes from a family of saxophone players. His name is Raul Johnson. His father was Sun Johnson, and he was a great alto player from the Swing Era and…
Did your father and your mother encourage you to a life in the arts? Because I know you were thinking about being a visual artist also?
